nodes.name: Gmail Inbound Poll
nodes.notes: Polls a DEDICATED inbox once a minute for is:unread. This credential is NOT 1Cgivoyjt7psAirH -- that one is the outbound sender and must stay outbound-only; the id above is a placeholder and the import will show this node unbound until the inbound credential is created and selected by hand. simple=false on purpose: the simplified output drops payload.headers, and Message-ID lives there. THE FAILURE MODE THAT KILLS THIS WORKFLOW SILENTLY: if the Google Cloud OAuth consent screen is left in Testing, the refresh token expires every 7 days, the poll starts failing, and leads pile up unread with nothing shouting about it. Publish the consent screen. See SETUP-RUNBOOK.md.

nodes.name: Parse Lead Email
nodes.notes: Verbatim copy of ops/n8n-gmail-inbound/parse-lead-email.node.js, which is what parse-lead-email.test.js runs (47 assertions). Edit the file, rebuild this workflow, re-import -- never hand-edit the node in the n8n UI, because then the tested body and the running body are different programs.

nodes.name: Parsed?
nodes.notes: TRUE -> record. FALSE -> the message is left UNREAD and untouched so a human sees it in the inbox. The only refusal this node body produces is a missing Message-ID, and a missing Message-ID is a message we cannot safely ingest at all, not one we can retry.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_public_key: $env.NEXUS_EMAIL_ENDPOINT_PUBLIC_KEY, p_external_event_id: $json.external_event_id, p_origin_verified: 'mailbox_read_oauth', p_payload_raw: $json.payload_raw, p_occurred_at: $json.occurred_at, p_normalized: $json.normalized_defect === null ? $json.normalized : null }) }}

nodes.name: Record Lead Event
nodes.notes: p_public_key comes from $env.NEXUS_EMAIL_ENDPOINT_PUBLIC_KEY and is NOT written into this file: a workflow JSON is exported, pasted and committed, and a key pasted into one has left the building. If that variable is unset the RPC is called with null and refuses -- the workflow fails loudly rather than writing a lead into the wrong tenant. p_normalized is sent ONLY when the local contract check passed; a defective normalized object makes the function raise, and this way the defect is recorded as a fact about the email instead of an exception.

nodes.name: Already Have This Email?
nodes.notes: A re-poll of the same Message-ID lands here. TRUE -> stop, without touching the stored row: re-promoting is harmless but re-rejecting is not, and neither is worth the risk for a row we already hold. The mail is still labelled and marked read, because the reason it was polled twice is usually that it never got marked read the first time.

nodes.name: Stop: Already Ingested
nodes.notes: Deliberately does nothing to the lead_event row.

nodes.name: A Real Customer We Can Reach?
nodes.notes: Reads the parse node rather than the RPC response, because the promotability decision was made where the evidence is. Requires pairedItem, which the Code node sets on every item it emits.

nodes.name: Promote To Lead
nodes.notes: Creates the lead the dealership actually sees.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_event_id: $('Record Lead Event').item.json.event_id, p_phase: 'REJECTED', p_reason: ('The email was received and is recorded, but it does not contain enough to contact anyone: ' + $('Parse Lead Email').item.json.normalized_defect + '. Nothing was inferred from the sender address on purpose. Subject: ' + ($('Parse Lead Email').item.json.subject || '(none)')) }) }}

nodes.name: Hold Without Promoting
nodes.notes: REJECTED, not QUARANTINED: this is a real delivery whose CONTENT was insufficient. The row stays visible as evidence that the marketplace's notification template does not carry a contactable customer -- which is a fact worth someone's attention, not a bug to hide.

nodes.name: Label As Ingested
nodes.notes: Label id comes from $env.NEXUS_EMAIL_INGESTED_LABEL_ID. onError continues so that a labelling failure never rolls back an ingestion that already succeeded -- the lead is the valuable thing here, the label is bookkeeping. The cost of that choice is an inbox that can drift out of step with the database; the Message-ID idempotency key is what makes the drift harmless.

nodes.name: Mark Read
nodes.notes: This is what stops the is:unread poll returning the same message forever. If it fails the message is re-polled and nexus_record_lead_event answers was_duplicate on the Message-ID, so the dealership is not handed the same person twice -- that database call, not this node, is the real guard.

main.node: A Real Customer We Can Reach?
